title: PMP 2026 Original Practice Question Bank
disclaimer: Independent educational practice material. Not official PMI questions and not copied from third-party simulators.

cases.title: Clinical AI Triage Pilot
cases.overview: A hospital network is piloting an AI-assisted triage service. Clinical safety rules and privacy controls must pass fixed gates, while interface workflows and model behavior require iterative testing with nurses and physicians. The sponsor wants a visible pilot in twelve weeks. Operations wants faster triage, finance wants lower staffing cost, and clinicians emphasize safety and fairness.
facts: Pilot in 12 weeks; safety evidence due in week 9
One patient group is underrepresented in training data
Target says improve triage, but no baseline or benefit owner exists
Only 35 percent of pilot nurses completed workflow training
questions: P1
Stakeholders use the same broad purpose but disagree on the outcomes that should determine pilot priorities.
PR1
Clinical controls are stable and mandatory, while user workflow and model performance require learning cycles.
B2
Data lineage, fairness testing, human review, and audit evidence are incomplete.
PR3
The project has a benefit statement but no baseline, target owner, or measurement process.
B7
Most nurses have not yet practiced the new workflow that will be required during the pilot.

cases.title: Remote Campus Microgrid
cases.overview: An industrial campus is installing a renewable microgrid before a fixed grid-connection window. The design is mostly stable, but a sole-source battery supplier has shown financial weakness. A nearby community is concerned about construction traffic and land use. Environmental approval requires evidence of lifecycle impacts and emergency controls.
facts: Battery equipment is 38 percent of project cost
Grid connection can occur only during a 10-day utility window
Two late financial filings and a negative credit alert
No public workshop has been held
Environmental permit condition is not yet linked to the work packages
questions: P4
The affected community is scheduled to receive only a final notice shortly before construction.
PR5
The sole-source battery supplier may not remain financially stable through delivery.
B5
Lifecycle environmental and community impacts have not been fully analyzed.
PR8
The utility connection dependency determines whether commissioning can occur this year.
B1
The project has no agreed escalation threshold for supplier, permit, or grid-window exposure.

cases.title: Digital Bank Onboarding
cases.overview: A retail bank is replacing its onboarding journey. Identity verification and regulatory evidence follow controlled milestones, while customer experience features are developed iteratively. Marketing has promised a public launch, compliance requires auditable consent, and operations expects no increase in manual review. A senior executive has requested an AI summary feature after scope approval.
facts: Consent and identity evidence are mandatory for release
AI summary is not linked to an approved outcome or acceptance criterion
Milestone or budget changes require steering approval
questions: P5
Marketing, operations, and compliance expectations cannot all be met without explicit trade-offs.
PR2
A new executive feature request is being treated informally outside the approved scope and traceability.
B3
The request affects controlled scope, budget, and the launch milestone.
PR7
Mandatory consent and identity evidence is at risk of being deferred until after release.
B8
A new privacy rule takes effect before the public launch.

cases.title: Transit Ticketing Modernization
cases.overview: A transit authority is modernizing mobile and station ticketing. The core fare engine and settlement controls are predictive, while the rider app is delivered iteratively. Two systems vendors dispute interface responsibility. A disability advocacy group says accessibility testing began too late. The fare-year date is fixed by public policy.
facts: Two critical user journeys fail current tests
Vendor dashboard and internal schedule show different integration dates
Station support teams have not received runbooks
questions: P2
The vendors and internal team blame one another and cite different interface agreements.
P4
A directly affected advocacy group was engaged only after major design decisions.
PR9
The executive dashboard and source schedules report different integration dates.
PR7
Accessibility quality requirements are not sufficiently measurable or complete.
PR10
Operations support readiness and runbooks are incomplete as transition approaches.

questions.stem: Use the Clinical AI Triage Pilot case information. Stakeholders use the same broad purpose but disagree on the outcomes that should determine pilot priorities. Which action should the project manager take before proceeding?
options: Continue delivery and postpone the alignment discussion until project closure.
Escalate the disagreement immediately without first clarifying the underlying assumptions.
Publish the existing vision again and require stakeholders to comply without discussion.
Facilitate agreement on measurable outcomes, success criteria, and decision principles before prioritizing work.
questions.rationale: A shared vision must be translated into observable outcomes and decision criteria before it can guide trade-offs. In this case, the project manager should facilitate agreement on measurable outcomes, success criteria, and decision principles before prioritizing work.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.task_title: Develop an integrated project management plan and plan delivery
questions.stem: Use the Clinical AI Triage Pilot case information. Clinical controls are stable and mandatory, while user workflow and model performance require learning cycles. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Exclude sustainability information because it is not a traditional scope, cost, or schedule measure.
Tailor a hybrid delivery approach that integrates predictive controls with iterative discovery and delivery.
Start execution before critical information requirements and decision thresholds are defined.
Use the same development approach for every component regardless of uncertainty or constraints.
questions.rationale: The development approach should match uncertainty and constraints rather than forcing all work into one method. In this case, the project manager should tailor a hybrid delivery approach that integrates predictive controls with iterative discovery and delivery.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Clinical AI Triage Pilot case information. Data lineage, fairness testing, human review, and audit evidence are incomplete. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Identify the applicable legal, ethical, security, and organizational compliance requirements and plan evidence and controls.
Assume audit readiness because team members say the controls were performed.
Release first and remediate the new requirement after customer feedback is collected.
Keep personal data indefinitely because storage is inexpensive.
questions.rationale: Responsible AI delivery requires explicit governance, data quality, human review, and auditable controls. In this case, the project manager should identify the applicable legal, ethical, security, and organizational compliance requirements and plan evidence and controls.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Clinical AI Triage Pilot case information. The project has a benefit statement but no baseline, target owner, or measurement process. What should the project manager do first?
options: Define the value components, benefit measures, baselines, targets, and ownership with key stakeholders.
Define benefit measures but leave ownership to be decided after closure.
Ignore declining usage because the schedule and budget remain within baseline.
Prioritize the request from the most senior stakeholder without comparing outcomes.
questions.rationale: Value-based delivery requires measurable outcomes and ownership, not only a broad benefit statement. In this case, the project manager should define the value components, benefit measures, baselines, targets, and ownership with key stakeholders.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Clinical AI Triage Pilot case information. Most nurses have not yet practiced the new workflow that will be required during the pilot. What should the project manager do first?
options: Ignore incentives that reward the old behavior.
Assess readiness and deliver role-based learning, practice, and support before the transition.
Accept private sponsor support without visible leadership action.
Treat resistance as a communication failure without investigating causes.
questions.rationale: Change readiness requires capability before people are expected to perform in the new way. In this case, the project manager should assess readiness and deliver role-based learning, practice, and support before the transition.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Remote Campus Microgrid case information. The affected community is scheduled to receive only a final notice shortly before construction. What should the project manager do first?
options: Focus only on the sponsor because the sponsor has the most formal authority.
Escalate resistance as noncompliance before understanding the stakeholder's concerns.
Use communication volume as the primary measure of stakeholder engagement.
Identify representative community stakeholders and establish early two-way engagement on impacts and concerns.
questions.rationale: Early engagement reduces surprises and builds trust with stakeholders who are directly affected by project outcomes. In this case, the project manager should identify representative community stakeholders and establish early two-way engagement on impacts and concerns.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Remote Campus Microgrid case information. The sole-source battery supplier may not remain financially stable through delivery. Which action should the project manager take before proceeding?
options: Ignore supplier financial risk until a delivery is actually missed.
Assess the exposure and implement appropriate responses such as safeguards, alternate sources, milestones, or contingency plans.
Direct the supplier to perform changed work before contractual approval.
Use a fixed-price contract when the scope cannot be defined and expect the supplier to absorb all uncertainty.
questions.rationale: Supplier risk should be actively managed through the procurement strategy and project risk process. In this case, the project manager should assess the exposure and implement appropriate responses such as safeguards, alternate sources, milestones, or contingency plans.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Remote Campus Microgrid case information. Lifecycle environmental and community impacts have not been fully analyzed. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Deploy an AI model without bias testing or human oversight.
Identify and analyze the sustainability risks across the lifecycle and integrate responses into design and governance decisions.
Keep risks as an unprioritized list without owners or responses.
Treat every risk with the same response regardless of tolerance or cost effectiveness.
questions.rationale: Sustainability risks affect long-term value, compliance, reputation, and stakeholder outcomes. In this case, the project manager should identify and analyze the sustainability risks across the lifecycle and integrate responses into design and governance decisions.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Remote Campus Microgrid case information. The utility connection dependency determines whether commissioning can occur this year. What should the project manager do first?
options: Change the schedule baseline without the required authorization.
Keep overlapping resource assignments and rely on overtime.
Coordinate the dependency, update the integrated schedule, and assess downstream impacts and options.
Fast track every activity regardless of dependency or risk.
questions.rationale: Cross-project dependencies must be actively coordinated and reflected in the schedule. In this case, the project manager should coordinate the dependency, update the integrated schedule, and assess downstream impacts and options.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Remote Campus Microgrid case information. The project has no agreed escalation threshold for supplier, permit, or grid-window exposure. Which action should the project manager take before proceeding?
options: Define escalation thresholds, paths, decision authorities, and required information with governance stakeholders.
Let each workstream decide its own approval authority.
Keep decision rights informal so leaders remain flexible.
Add more governance meetings without defining decisions or owners.
questions.rationale: Clear thresholds prevent both under-escalation and unnecessary escalation. In this case, the project manager should define escalation thresholds, paths, decision authorities, and required information with governance stakeholders.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Digital Bank Onboarding case information. Marketing, operations, and compliance expectations cannot all be met without explicit trade-offs. What should the project manager do first?
options: Accept all urgent requests and rely on overtime to resolve prioritization.
Document the constraints and feasible trade-offs, then facilitate stakeholder agreement on priorities and decision criteria.
Ask the team to satisfy every expectation even though the constraints conflict.
Remove the inexperienced stakeholder from decisions instead of mentoring and clarifying governance.
questions.rationale: Competing expectations should be made explicit and reconciled before the team commits to an infeasible solution. In this case, the project manager should document the constraints and feasible trade-offs, then facilitate stakeholder agreement on priorities and decision criteria.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Digital Bank Onboarding case information. A new executive feature request is being treated informally outside the approved scope and traceability. What should the project manager do first?
options: Identify and assess the accumulated scope changes, then apply the agreed change-control process.
Estimate large backlog items without decomposing them.
Treat exclusions and assumptions as unnecessary details.
Reject every change request because the original scope was approved.
questions.rationale: Uncontrolled small changes create scope creep; their cumulative impact must be made visible and governed. In this case, the project manager should identify and assess the accumulated scope changes, then apply the agreed change-control process.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Digital Bank Onboarding case information. The request affects controlled scope, budget, and the launch milestone. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Skip documentation and authority during an emergency.
Log the request, analyze impacts and options, and submit it to the authorized change decision body.
Treat an approved change as complete without updating plans or execution.
Implement the request immediately and document it after delivery.
questions.rationale: Integrated change control preserves authorized commitments and informed decision-making. In this case, the project manager should log the request, analyze impacts and options, and submit it to the authorized change decision body.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.task_title: Plan and optimize quality of products and deliverables
questions.stem: Use the Digital Bank Onboarding case information. Mandatory consent and identity evidence is at risk of being deferred until after release. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Integrate compliance evidence and quality verification into the definition of complete and the release process.
Correct each repeated defect without investigating its source.
Accept the deliverable because it was completed on schedule even though criteria are not met.
Continue work using subjective quality terms and decide acceptance at the end.
questions.rationale: Mandatory evidence is part of quality and completion, not an administrative activity that can be deferred safely. In this case, the project manager should integrate compliance evidence and quality verification into the definition of complete and the release process.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Digital Bank Onboarding case information. A new privacy rule takes effect before the public launch. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Continue using the original business case after major economic assumptions change.
Assess the impact on scope, backlog, compliance, value, risk, and timing, then reprioritize and govern the response.
Keep a sole-source plan unchanged during a serious geopolitical disruption.
Copy a competitor feature without assessing strategy, value, or risk.
questions.rationale: External changes should be translated into project impacts and decisions rather than treated as background information. In this case, the project manager should assess the impact on scope, backlog, compliance, value, risk, and timing, then reprioritize and govern the response.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Transit Ticketing Modernization case information. The vendors and internal team blame one another and cite different interface agreements. Which action should the project manager take before proceeding?
options: Bring the parties together around the contract, approved requirements, and objective evidence to identify the source and agree on recovery.
Move the disputed work to a later phase without resolving the relationship or decision issue.
Record the conflict as a risk but take no resolution action.
Replace one of the people involved so the conflict ends quickly.
questions.rationale: Conflict with an external party should be resolved using facts, agreements, and shared recovery objectives rather than public blame. In this case, the project manager should bring the parties together around the contract, approved requirements, and objective evidence to identify the source and agree on recovery.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Transit Ticketing Modernization case information. A directly affected advocacy group was engaged only after major design decisions. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Use communication volume as the primary measure of stakeholder engagement.
Delay community or user engagement until the solution is nearly complete.
Identify representative community stakeholders and establish early two-way engagement on impacts and concerns.
Focus only on the sponsor because the sponsor has the most formal authority.
questions.rationale: Early engagement reduces surprises and builds trust with stakeholders who are directly affected by project outcomes. In this case, the project manager should identify representative community stakeholders and establish early two-way engagement on impacts and concerns.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Transit Ticketing Modernization case information. The executive dashboard and source schedules report different integration dates. What should the project manager do first?
options: Keep unused report sections because the template has always included them.
Give every audience the same level of detail regardless of its decisions.
Accept subjective percentage complete when objective evidence disagrees.
Reconcile the source data, correct the artifacts, and establish a controlled source of truth and update process.
questions.rationale: Conflicting artifacts undermine decisions; status must be based on reconciled, current information. In this case, the project manager should reconcile the source data, correct the artifacts, and establish a controlled source of truth and update process.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.task_title: Plan and optimize quality of products and deliverables
questions.stem: Use the Transit Ticketing Modernization case information. Accessibility quality requirements are not sufficiently measurable or complete. Which action should the project manager take before proceeding?
options: Use final inspection as the only quality activity.
Reduce prevention activities because they do not create visible deliverables.
Ignore a point outside control limits because the average is acceptable.
Gather measurable quality and acceptance requirements with the relevant stakeholders before more work proceeds.
questions.rationale: Quality must be defined in testable terms; broad adjectives cannot guide prevention or acceptance. In this case, the project manager should gather measurable quality and acceptance requirements with the relevant stakeholders before more work proceeds.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: Use the Transit Ticketing Modernization case information. Operations support readiness and runbooks are incomplete as transition approaches. Which action should the project manager take before proceeding?
options: Close the project on the planned date even when acceptance and transition criteria are not met.
Complete and validate the transition to operations before releasing the project team.
Transfer unresolved critical defects to operations without agreement.
Abandon closure activities when the project is terminated early.
questions.rationale: A deliverable is not fully transitioned until the receiving organization can operate and support it. In this case, the project manager should complete and validate the transition to operations before releasing the project team.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: During the omnichannel retail launch, what should the project manager do first after reviewing the resource-capacity exhibit?
options: Validate the demand and availability for week(s) 2, 3, then level, resequence, or add capability as appropriate.
Require overtime in every week without analyzing priorities.
Keep the plan because total four-week capacity is sufficient.
Remove quality activities from the overloaded periods.

questions.stem: A project manager is leading the renewable microgrid installation. The PMO requests thirty weekly metrics, but several do not support any identified decision and the reporting effort is reducing delivery capacity. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Give executives the same technical detail used by delivery teams.
Measure communication effectiveness by the number of messages sent.
Clarify stakeholder information and governance decision needs, then agree on a concise reporting set and cadence.
Send all available data to every stakeholder at the same frequency.
questions.rationale: Communication should be designed around decisions and stakeholder needs rather than maximizing the amount of data produced. The best response is to clarify stakeholder information and governance decision needs, then agree on a concise reporting set and cadence.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: During the supply-chain analytics product, which is being delivered through a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control, an adaptive team can reprioritize backlog items, but a proposed change also alters a regulated release milestone and contract commitment. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Use backlog prioritization for flexible product scope and formal change control for the controlled milestone and contract impacts.
Update the baseline before the change decision is made.
Reject every change because a baseline already exists.
Follow an unauthorized direction because it came from a functional manager.
questions.rationale: Hybrid projects distinguish between team-level adaptive authority and changes to controlled external commitments. The best response is to use backlog prioritization for flexible product scope and formal change control for the controlled milestone and contract impacts.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: The regional hospital scheduling platform must meet a winter peak-season go-live while protecting patient privacy and clinical safety controls. A threat can be eliminated by changing the solution so the risky component is no longer needed. The team has little contingency remaining. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Close a risk after a response is planned without monitoring triggers or residual exposure.
Use risk avoidance if the change is feasible and the resulting trade-offs are acceptable.
Treat every risk with the same response regardless of tolerance or cost effectiveness.
Call a response avoidance when it only reduces probability.
questions.rationale: Avoidance removes the threat by changing the plan rather than merely reducing probability or impact. The best response is to use risk avoidance if the change is feasible and the resulting trade-offs are acceptable.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.task_title: Develop an integrated project management plan and plan delivery
questions.stem: A project manager is leading the community housing development. Early estimates for a complex initiative have wide uncertainty, yet the sponsor asks for a single precise commitment. The team has little contingency remaining. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Select a delivery approach only because the organization used it on the last project.
Exclude sustainability information because it is not a traditional scope, cost, or schedule measure.
Start execution before critical information requirements and decision thresholds are defined.
Provide an estimate range with assumptions and use progressive elaboration as information improves.
questions.rationale: Planning should communicate uncertainty honestly and improve estimates over time rather than creating false precision. The best response is to provide an estimate range with assumptions and use progressive elaboration as information improves.

questions.stem: During the telecom network expansion, which is being delivered through a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control, a team member adds a useful feature that was not requested because there appears to be spare time in the iteration. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Accept useful extra features because they may improve customer satisfaction.
Reject every change request because the original scope was approved.
Stop the unapproved addition and evaluate it through the appropriate backlog prioritization or change process.
Begin detailed design before stakeholders agree on scope boundaries.
questions.rationale: Gold plating creates risk and consumes capacity even when the added feature seems beneficial. The best response is to stop the unapproved addition and evaluate it through the appropriate backlog prioritization or change process.

Prioritize the request from the most senior stakeholder without comparing outcomes.

questions.stem: The warehouse robotics deployment must meet the annual demand peak while protecting safety, vendor integration, and workforce adoption. Virtual meetings are dominated by two senior specialists, while quieter team members rarely contribute even when their expertise is relevant. The sponsor has asked the team to protect the committed date. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Measure leadership effectiveness only by the number of tasks completed.
Require additional overtime until the milestone is achieved.
Wait for the sponsor to notice the team's impediment.
Monitor participation and ask the team to refine working agreements that support balanced input.
Use inclusive facilitation techniques and create psychological safety so all perspectives can be heard.
questions.rationale: The project manager should actively support varied experiences and perspectives rather than equating silence with agreement. The strongest pair is to use inclusive facilitation techniques and create psychological safety so all perspectives can be heard. and then monitor participation and ask the team to refine working agreements that support balanced input.

questions.stem: During the government tax-filing portal, which is being delivered through an adaptive product approach with short iterations and frequent stakeholder feedback, the sponsor supports the project privately but does not visibly reinforce the change when functional leaders resist. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Use the same change approach regardless of organizational culture.
Engage the sponsor to build an active change coalition and provide visible, consistent sponsorship.
Ignore incentives that reward the old behavior.
Schedule training after the old process is no longer available.
questions.rationale: Visible sponsorship and aligned leadership are critical to organizational adoption. The best response is to engage the sponsor to build an active change coalition and provide visible, consistent sponsorship.

questions.stem: On the telecom network expansion, the team is using a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control. The development and quality leads disagree about whether a deliverable is complete because they interpreted the acceptance criteria differently. A recent stakeholder survey shows declining confidence. Which action should the project manager take before proceeding?
options: Avoid the issue and wait for the team to resolve it without support.
Facilitate a fact-based discussion to compare interpretations, identify the source of the conflict, and agree on the criteria.
Send a general reminder about professionalism without addressing the specific conflict.
Escalate the disagreement to the sponsor before the parties have discussed the facts.
questions.rationale: The project manager should diagnose the conflict and help the parties reach an agreed resolution before escalating or imposing a solution. The best response is to facilitate a fact-based discussion to compare interpretations, identify the source of the conflict, and agree on the criteria.

What is the best next action for the project manager?

Treat resistance as a communication failure without investigating causes.
Limit change impact analysis to technical system changes.
Ignore incentives that reward the old behavior.
questions.rationale: Change readiness requires capability before people are expected to perform in the new way. The best response is to assess readiness and deliver role-based learning, practice, and support before the transition.

questions.stem: The airport baggage-handling replacement must meet the summer travel peak while protecting safety certification and multiple systems vendors. Retrospectives produce useful notes, but the same mistakes recur because the notes are stored in personal files and never used in planning. A recent stakeholder survey shows declining confidence. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Treat retrospective notes as complete knowledge transfer even when no action is assigned.
Capture the learning in an accessible repository and integrate agreed actions into working practices and future planning.
Place sensitive information in a broadly accessible collaboration folder.
Ask the departing specialist to upload files without validating understanding.
questions.rationale: Knowledge creates value only when it is accessible, owned, and applied. The best response is to capture the learning in an accessible repository and integrate agreed actions into working practices and future planning.

Delay correcting status information until the next formal governance meeting.
Accept subjective percentage complete when objective evidence disagrees.
Define and tailor a concise set of metrics that supports project decisions, outcomes, and governance thresholds.
questions.rationale: Status evaluation should enable decisions and reflect progress, value, risk, and commitments rather than maximize metric volume. The best response is to define and tailor a concise set of metrics that supports project decisions, outcomes, and governance thresholds.

questions.stem: On the factory automation program, the team is using a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control. A production incident requires urgent action, and the normal change board will not meet in time. The latest forecast shows that one constraint cannot be met without a trade-off. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Follow an unauthorized direction because it came from a functional manager.
Use the defined emergency-change path with appropriate authority, documentation, risk assessment, and retrospective review.
Treat an approved change as complete without updating plans or execution.
Use backlog authority to alter regulated milestones or contracts without approval.
questions.rationale: Urgency may require a faster path, but it does not eliminate governance, traceability, or accountability. The best response is to use the defined emergency-change path with appropriate authority, documentation, risk assessment, and retrospective review.

questions.stem: The digital onboarding service for a retail bank must meet a public product launch in twelve weeks while protecting privacy, accessibility, and anti-fraud requirements. The project tracks total spend but cannot explain which work, risks, or commitments are driving the latest increase. What should the project manager do first?
options: Establish spend tracking by meaningful categories and reconcile actuals, commitments, forecast, and remaining work.
Combine all reserves so the project manager can use them without approval.
Use the maximum possible risk loss as the expected monetary value.
Report current spend as the final forecast without analyzing remaining work.
questions.rationale: Useful financial control links spending to work, commitments, risk, and forecast rather than reporting only a total. The best response is to establish spend tracking by meaningful categories and reconcile actuals, commitments, forecast, and remaining work.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: During the factory automation program, which is being delivered through an adaptive product approach with short iterations and frequent stakeholder feedback, important decisions stall because workstream leads do not know who recommends, approves, contributes, or must be informed. The latest forecast shows that one constraint cannot be met without a trade-off. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Establish clear decision rights, roles, and escalation paths in the project governance structure.
Hide unfavorable information until a solution has been implemented.
Remove mandatory controls to make a small project faster.
Add more governance meetings without defining decisions or owners.
questions.rationale: Governance should make authority, accountability, and information flow explicit so decisions are timely and defensible. The best response is to establish clear decision rights, roles, and escalation paths in the project governance structure.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: The supply-chain analytics product must meet the annual planning cycle while protecting incomplete supplier data and changing trade conditions. Use scope completion as the only measure of value.
Choose the option with the most features regardless of learning or risk.
Establish a benefits owner, measurement process, cadence, and post-transition responsibility.
questions.rationale: A measurement system needs ownership and continuity beyond delivery. The best response is to establish a benefits owner, measurement process, cadence, and post-transition responsibility.

questions.stem: On the customer-support AI assistant, the team is using an adaptive product approach with short iterations and frequent stakeholder feedback. options: Reassess the stakeholder's influence, impact, interests, and preferred engagement approach.
Classify a stakeholder as low interest solely because the person misses meetings.
Delay community or user engagement until the solution is nearly complete.
Use communication volume as the primary measure of stakeholder engagement.
questions.rationale: Low meeting attendance does not mean low influence or low impact; engagement must be based on analysis, not assumptions. The best response is to reassess the stakeholder's influence, impact, interests, and preferred engagement approach.

questions.stem: On the community housing development, the team is using iterative delivery within integrated stage-gate and governance controls. options: Use sponsor pressure as a substitute for customer or governance acceptance.
Resolve the claim, verify handover and acceptance, and formally close the procurement before project closure.
Abandon closure activities when the project is terminated early.
Transfer unresolved critical defects to operations without agreement.
questions.rationale: Open contractual obligations are closure blockers even when the physical deliverable is present. The best response is to resolve the claim, verify handover and acceptance, and formally close the procurement before project closure.

questions.stem: A project manager is leading the municipal transport ticketing modernization. Use the same leadership style regardless of team maturity or context.
Shift toward a delegating and supporting style while maintaining clear outcomes and guardrails.
Escalate normal team decisions to governance rather than clarifying boundaries.
questions.rationale: Over-directing a mature team reduces ownership; effective leadership adapts to the team's capability. The best response is to shift toward a delegating and supporting style while maintaining clear outcomes and guardrails.

questions.stem: A project manager is leading the municipal transport ticketing modernization. The team is meeting dates only by sustained overtime, and quality defects and sick leave are increasing. Make every routine decision personally so quality remains consistent.
Rebalance commitments and capacity with the team and stakeholders to restore a sustainable pace.

questions.task_title: Develop an integrated project management plan and plan delivery
questions.stem: A project manager is leading the national identity verification service. Workstream plans use different assumptions and dates, and several dependencies are missing from the consolidated forecast. The latest forecast shows that one constraint cannot be met without a trade-off. What should the project manager do first?
options: Update the integrated plan and assign owners for cross-workstream dependencies.
Treat the project charter as a complete integrated project management plan.
Exclude sustainability information because it is not a traditional scope, cost, or schedule measure.
Integrate the subsidiary plans, reconcile assumptions, and analyze dependencies, gaps, and continued business value.
Select a delivery approach only because the organization used it on the last project.
questions.rationale: An integrated plan must be coherent across scope, schedule, resources, risk, finance, and governance. The strongest pair is to integrate the subsidiary plans, reconcile assumptions, and analyze dependencies, gaps, and continued business value. and then update the integrated plan and assign owners for cross-workstream dependencies.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: During the customer-support AI assistant, which is being delivered through a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control, several team members are unsure who owns testing, data migration, and operational readiness, and important work is being duplicated. A governance review is scheduled within five business days. What should the project manager do first?
options: Use the same leadership style regardless of team maturity or context.
Measure leadership effectiveness only by the number of tasks completed.
Facilitate agreement on clear roles, responsibilities, and interfaces for the affected work.
Make every routine decision personally so quality remains consistent.
questions.rationale: Clear accountability and interfaces reduce duplication, gaps, and conflict. The best response is to facilitate agreement on clear roles, responsibilities, and interfaces for the affected work.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: The water-treatment plant upgrade must meet a regulator-defined compliance date while protecting environmental discharge limits and community concerns. Sensitive project knowledge must be shared with authorized teams while remaining protected from broader access. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Use an access-controlled repository and define ownership, classification, and approved transfer methods.
Use meeting attendance as proof that knowledge was transferred.
Ask the departing specialist to upload files without validating understanding.
Place sensitive information in a broadly accessible collaboration folder.
questions.rationale: Knowledge transfer must balance accessibility with security and compliance requirements. The best response is to use an access-controlled repository and define ownership, classification, and approved transfer methods.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: The mine rehabilitation initiative must meet a license-renewal review while protecting environmental restoration and local employment commitments. A new privacy requirement takes effect before the planned release and changes how customer data may be collected and retained. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Treat AI bias, data lineage, and human oversight as optional technical preferences.
Release first and remediate the new requirement after customer feedback is collected.
Confirm the requirement with qualified stakeholders, assess project impacts, and update the compliance and delivery approach.
Begin safety-critical work before required authorization because the schedule is fixed.
questions.rationale: A new mandatory requirement must be analyzed and incorporated; it cannot be deferred merely to protect the original plan. The best response is to confirm the requirement with qualified stakeholders, assess project impacts, and update the compliance and delivery approach.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: The omnichannel retail launch must meet the holiday sales period while protecting inventory integration and peak-load performance. The team cannot progress because an organizational policy requires an approval that no team member is authorized to obtain. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Replace quieter team members with more assertive participants.
Measure leadership effectiveness only by the number of tasks completed.
Make every routine decision personally so quality remains consistent.
Represent the team's need to the accountable authority and work to remove or expedite the organizational impediment.
questions.rationale: A project leader should advocate for the team and remove obstacles that are outside the team's authority. The best response is to represent the team's need to the accountable authority and work to remove or expedite the organizational impediment.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: During the carbon-reporting data platform, which is being delivered through a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control, executives, the product team, and operations require different levels of detail from the same status data. Which action should the project manager take before proceeding?
options: Keep unused report sections because the template has always included them.
Tailor status artifacts and views to each audience while preserving consistent underlying data.
Give every audience the same level of detail regardless of its decisions.
Confirm that each view supports the audience's decisions and responsibilities.
Analyze cost, schedule, quality, and value separately without reconciling implications.
questions.rationale: Artifact tailoring improves usefulness without creating different versions of project truth. The strongest pair is to tailor status artifacts and views to each audience while preserving consistent underlying data. and then confirm that each view supports the audience's decisions and responsibilities.

questions.stem: The enterprise resource planning transformation must meet the next fiscal year while protecting business-process change and data migration. The team is about to disband and has not consolidated lessons, decisions, and reusable assets. The sponsor has asked the team to protect the committed date. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Release the team before knowledge, financial, and contractual closure is complete.
Abandon closure activities when the project is terminated early.
Facilitate final lessons learned, archive relevant knowledge, and update organizational process assets.
Close the project on the planned date even when acceptance and transition criteria are not met.
questions.rationale: Closure should preserve knowledge and improve future performance rather than allow learning to disappear with the team. The best response is to facilitate final lessons learned, archive relevant knowledge, and update organizational process assets.

questions.stem: During the municipal transport ticketing modernization, which is being delivered through iterative delivery within integrated stage-gate and governance controls, the project will use an AI capability, but data lineage, bias testing, human oversight, and audit evidence have not been defined. options: Identify the applicable legal, ethical, security, and organizational compliance requirements and plan evidence and controls.
Assume audit readiness because team members say the controls were performed.
Accept supplier work without required sustainability or compliance evidence.
Release first and remediate the new requirement after customer feedback is collected.
questions.rationale: Responsible AI delivery requires explicit governance, data quality, human review, and auditable controls. The best response is to identify the applicable legal, ethical, security, and organizational compliance requirements and plan evidence and controls.

questions.stem: On the airport baggage-handling replacement, the team is using a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control. The sponsor and customer disagree about whether a deliverable satisfies the approved scope. What is the best next action for the project manager?

Let each team lead approve small scope requests independently.
Trace the deliverable to agreed requirements and acceptance criteria, then facilitate resolution of any ambiguity.

questions.stem: The national identity verification service must meet a staged national rollout while protecting privacy, inclusion, and cross-agency governance. A project reports high percentage complete, but earned value, defect, and acceptance data indicate that critical deliverables are behind. What should the project manager do first?
options: Give every audience the same level of detail regardless of its decisions.
Accept subjective percentage complete when objective evidence disagrees.
Analyze cost, schedule, quality, and value separately without reconciling implications.
Assess progress using objective completion and performance evidence rather than subjective percent complete.
questions.rationale: Reliable status uses measurable completion and performance data, especially when subjective reporting conflicts with evidence. The best response is to assess progress using objective completion and performance evidence rather than subjective percent complete.

questions.stem: During the vaccine cold-chain monitoring system, which is being delivered through an adaptive product approach with short iterations and frequent stakeholder feedback, small requests are being accepted informally by different team leads, and the cumulative impact is now affecting the date and budget. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Treat exclusions and assumptions as unnecessary details.
Identify and assess the accumulated scope changes, then apply the agreed change-control process.
Estimate large backlog items without decomposing them.
Use the sponsor's opinion as the only acceptance criterion.
questions.rationale: Uncontrolled small changes create scope creep; their cumulative impact must be made visible and governed. The best response is to identify and assess the accumulated scope changes, then apply the agreed change-control process.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: On the customer-support AI assistant, the team is using a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control. The schedule, risk register, and executive dashboard show different dates and statuses for the same milestone. Which action should the project manager take before proceeding?
options: Communicate the corrected status and prevent recurrence through ownership and review rules.
Reconcile the source data, correct the artifacts, and establish a controlled source of truth and update process.
Analyze cost, schedule, quality, and value separately without reconciling implications.
Accept subjective percentage complete when objective evidence disagrees.
Use activity counts as the only project-status measure.
questions.rationale: Conflicting artifacts undermine decisions; status must be based on reconciled, current information. questions.stem: On the supply-chain analytics product, the team is using a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control. Identify the operational knowledge required and complete a structured transfer with the receiving team.
Place sensitive information in a broadly accessible collaboration folder.

questions.stem: During the renewable microgrid installation, which is being delivered through a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control, the estimate includes quantified responses for identified risks and a separate allowance for unknown uncertainty, but both have been placed in one project-manager-controlled reserve. Rebaseline the budget immediately whenever a variance appears.
Use management reserve for identified risks before contingency reserve is considered.
questions.rationale: Reserve classification affects the baseline, performance reporting, and decision authority. The best response is to separate contingency reserve for identified risks within the cost baseline from management reserve outside the baseline under governance control.

questions.stem: The factory automation program must meet a planned maintenance shutdown while protecting worker safety and production continuity. Assume operations can learn the service after the project team is released.
Accept the supplier deliverable before maintainability knowledge is transferred.

A capable cross-functional team waits for the project manager to approve routine delivery decisions, creating delays and frustration. What should the project manager do first?

Wait for the sponsor to notice the team's impediment.
Clarify decision boundaries and empower the team to make routine decisions within agreed constraints.

questions.stem: A project manager is leading the omnichannel retail launch. The team changes its process frequently but has no baseline or measure to tell whether the changes improve performance. What should the project manager do first?
options: Ignore prior lessons because every project is unique.
Repeat reminders instead of investigating the cause of recurring defects.
Define a relevant process or outcome measure before testing the next improvement.
Mandate an enterprise-wide change after one isolated success.
questions.rationale: Improvement requires feedback and measurement, not change for its own sake. The best response is to define a relevant process or outcome measure before testing the next improvement.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: The vaccine cold-chain monitoring system must meet the next immunization campaign while protecting cross-border procurement and data reliability. Several departments submit urgent requests and each assumes its work will be delivered first. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Avoid discussing trade-offs until a constraint is actually missed.
Treat mandatory compliance evidence as an optional product preference.
Change the baseline before stakeholders have agreed on the desired outcome.
Establish transparent prioritization criteria based on value, risk, dependencies, and mandatory constraints.
questions.rationale: Common decision criteria align expectations more effectively than accepting requests in order of seniority or volume. The best response is to establish transparent prioritization criteria based on value, risk, dependencies, and mandatory constraints.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: On the supply-chain analytics product, the team is using a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control. The team has a list of uncertain events but has not assessed probability, impact, proximity, or response priority. Which action should the project manager take before proceeding?
options: Keep risks as an unprioritized list without owners or responses.
Deploy an AI model without bias testing or human oversight.
Close a risk after a response is planned without monitoring triggers or residual exposure.
Perform qualitative or quantitative analysis appropriate to the project and prioritize the risks.
questions.rationale: A list becomes actionable only when risks are analyzed, owned, and connected to responses and monitoring. The best response is to perform qualitative or quantitative analysis appropriate to the project and prioritize the risks.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: A project manager is leading the adaptive learning platform. A team member repeatedly interrupts colleagues and dismisses their input during planning sessions, contrary to the team charter. The project must preserve mandatory compliance and safety outcomes. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Replace one of the people involved so the conflict ends quickly.
Address the behavior promptly and respectfully, reference the agreed ground rules, and seek commitment to corrective behavior.
Send a general reminder about professionalism without addressing the specific conflict.
Avoid the issue and wait for the team to resolve it without support.
questions.rationale: Ground-rule violations should be managed directly and constructively so psychological safety and team effectiveness are restored. The best response is to address the behavior promptly and respectfully, reference the agreed ground rules, and seek commitment to corrective behavior.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: On the vaccine cold-chain monitoring system, the team is using an adaptive product approach with short iterations and frequent stakeholder feedback. A customer expects a feature in the next release even though it was not included in the agreed scope or prioritized backlog. What should the project manager do first?
options: Hide a likely delay until the team has missed the milestone.
Keep the original benefit target even when evidence shows it is no longer feasible.
Confirm the underlying need, explain the current commitment, and route the request through the appropriate prioritization or change process.
Promise the requested feature immediately to preserve the relationship.
questions.rationale: Expectation management combines listening, transparency, and the agreed control process rather than an immediate yes or no. The best response is to confirm the underlying need, explain the current commitment, and route the request through the appropriate prioritization or change process.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: A project manager is leading the adaptive learning platform. Two workstream leads are competing for the same specialist and each says its milestone is the top priority. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Analyze the interests, dependencies, and impact of the resource conflict, then facilitate a collaborative resolution.
Replace one of the people involved so the conflict ends quickly.
Move the disputed work to a later phase without resolving the relationship or decision issue.
Avoid the issue and wait for the team to resolve it without support.
questions.rationale: A durable resolution considers project-wide priorities and the underlying interests rather than simply splitting the resource or choosing a favorite. The best response is to analyze the interests, dependencies, and impact of the resource conflict, then facilitate a collaborative resolution.

questions.stem: During the factory automation program, which is being delivered through an adaptive product approach with short iterations and frequent stakeholder feedback, a defect trend continues despite repeated reminders to be careful. What is the best next action for the project manager?
options: Record the lesson without assigning an action or owner.
Measure improvement only by whether the team likes the new process.
Keep a proven checklist only in the original team's private workspace.
Use root-cause analysis and a structured improvement cycle to change the system that produces the defect.
questions.rationale: Reminders target behavior superficially; durable improvement addresses causes, process, and feedback. The best response is to use root-cause analysis and a structured improvement cycle to change the system that produces the defect.

questions.stem: The mine rehabilitation initiative must meet a license-renewal review while protecting environmental restoration and local employment commitments. options: Select a noncompliant shortcut when the financial benefit appears larger than the potential fine.
Begin safety-critical work before required authorization because the schedule is fixed.
Keep personal data indefinitely because storage is inexpensive.
Stop or defer the affected work until required safety controls and authorization are in place.
questions.rationale: Mandatory safety compliance is a release or work condition, not a risk that can be accepted informally. The best response is to stop or defer the affected work until required safety controls and authorization are in place.

Follow ethical and organizational reporting obligations and escalate the control failure through the defined governance path.

Measure schedule variance against an unapproved draft.
Hide a forecasted delay until the milestone is missed.
Ignore a dependent project's milestone because it is outside the project boundary.

questions.stem: The factory automation program must meet a planned maintenance shutdown while protecting worker safety and production continuity. A major market or regulatory change weakens one of the assumptions used to define the original project vision. What should the project manager do first?

Ask the sponsor to select a feature without first agreeing on the outcome it should support.
Continue delivery and postpone the alignment discussion until project closure.
Assess the impact with key stakeholders and update the shared vision if the intended value or feasible outcome has changed.

questions.stem: During the telecom network expansion, which is being delivered through a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control, the team is blocked by an approval owned by another department and cannot remove the obstacle itself. Track the intervention until the blocker is removed or an alternative is authorized.
Escalate without explaining impact, urgency, or the decision needed.
Engage or escalate to the accountable owner with clear impact, urgency, and the decision or action needed.
Continue temporary fixes without investigating recurrence.
questions.rationale: The project manager should remove or minimize impediments by involving the party with the required authority. Accept private sponsor support without visible leadership action.

Limit change impact analysis to technical system changes.

Tailor sponsor engagement to concise decision-focused information, thresholds, and scheduled decision points.

questions.stem: On the adaptive learning platform, the team is using a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control. A previously identified risk has occurred and is now blocking a critical activity. What should the project manager do first?

questions.stem: The government tax-filing portal must meet the statutory filing season while protecting security, accessibility, and high-volume demand. Reconnect the delivered work and upcoming priorities to the agreed vision and intended outcomes with stakeholders.
Ask the sponsor to select a feature without first agreeing on the outcome it should support.
Measure success only by the percentage of scope completed.

questions.stem: A project manager is leading the digital onboarding service for a retail bank. Keep a pending change confidential from teams whose work depends on the outcome.
Update the baseline before the change decision is made.
Implement the request immediately and document it after delivery.

questions.stem: During the pharmaceutical packaging line, which is being delivered through a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control, a large backlog contains broad items that cannot be estimated, tested, or completed within a delivery cycle. questions.stem: During the vaccine cold-chain monitoring system, which is being delivered through an adaptive product approach with short iterations and frequent stakeholder feedback, a risk response transfers financial exposure to an insurer, but operational and reputational impacts would still remain with the organization. Ignore positive risks and opportunities until they happen.
Document the transferred portion and actively manage the residual operational and reputational risks.

Level resources and then analyze the effect on the critical path and milestone dates.

A project-developed checklist has reduced defects, but the learning remains only in the project team's workspace. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Ignore prior lessons because every project is unique.
Record the lesson without assigning an action or owner.
Mandate an enterprise-wide change after one isolated success.
Validate the practice and update the appropriate organizational process asset or shared repository.
questions.rationale: Proven learning should be made accessible beyond the originating project. The best response is to validate the practice and update the appropriate organizational process asset or shared repository.

questions.stem: During the omnichannel retail launch, which is being delivered through an adaptive product approach with short iterations and frequent stakeholder feedback, a retrospective identifies a recurring cause of rework, but the improvement idea has no owner, due date, or follow-up measure. Mandate an enterprise-wide change after one isolated success.
questions.rationale: Continuous improvement converts learning into owned action, evidence, and updated practice. questions.task_title: Plan and optimize quality of products and deliverables
questions.stem: The airport baggage-handling replacement must meet the summer travel peak while protecting safety certification and multiple systems vendors. options: Gather measurable quality and acceptance requirements with the relevant stakeholders before more work proceeds.
Accept the deliverable because it was completed on schedule even though criteria are not met.
Correct each repeated defect without investigating its source.

questions.rationale: Quality must be defined in testable terms; broad adjectives cannot guide prevention or acceptance. The best response is to gather measurable quality and acceptance requirements with the relevant stakeholders before more work proceeds.

questions.stem: During the insurance claims automation service, which is being delivered through iterative delivery within integrated stage-gate and governance controls, two senior stakeholders support the project but promote incompatible solution directions, and the team is receiving conflicting instructions. questions.stem: A project manager is leading the insurance claims automation service. A newly appointed executive interprets the project purpose differently from the team and begins requesting work that does not support the original outcomes. The sponsor has asked the team to protect the committed date. What should the project manager do first?
options: Continue delivery and postpone the alignment discussion until project closure.
Measure success only by the percentage of scope completed.
Ask the sponsor to select a feature without first agreeing on the outcome it should support.
Revisit the vision with key stakeholders, surface the different assumptions, and confirm or update the shared direction.
questions.rationale: The project manager should resolve the divergence in meaning before accepting new work or enforcing the old interpretation. The best response is to revisit the vision with key stakeholders, surface the different assumptions, and confirm or update the shared direction.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: During the telecom network expansion, which is being delivered through iterative delivery within integrated stage-gate and governance controls, the internal team and a supplier blame each other for a late integration, and both cite different versions of the interface agreement. Several stakeholders are working across different time zones. What should the project manager do first?
options: Bring the parties together around the contract, approved requirements, and objective evidence to identify the source and agree on recovery.
Escalate the disagreement to the sponsor before the parties have discussed the facts.
Force a decision based only on the project manager's positional authority.
Avoid the issue and wait for the team to resolve it without support.
questions.rationale: Conflict with an external party should be resolved using facts, agreements, and shared recovery objectives rather than public blame. The best response is to bring the parties together around the contract, approved requirements, and objective evidence to identify the source and agree on recovery.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.task_title: Develop an integrated project management plan and plan delivery
questions.stem: The mobile payments platform must meet a partner launch event while protecting cybersecurity and transaction resilience. The project will construct a standardized facility using mature technology, approved designs, and a fixed completion date. Which action should the project manager take before proceeding?
options: Select a delivery approach only because the organization used it on the last project.
Let teams continue using the original plan after an approved change.
Use a primarily predictive approach with detailed planning, baselines, and controlled changes.
Treat the project charter as a complete integrated project management plan.
questions.rationale: Stable requirements and strong sequencing dependencies generally support predictive planning. The best response is to use a primarily predictive approach with detailed planning, baselines, and controlled changes.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: On the telecom network expansion, the team is using a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control. Customer satisfaction falls after an early release even though the team delivered all planned stories. A recent stakeholder survey shows declining confidence. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Keep the original benefit target even when evidence shows it is no longer feasible.
Allow different acceptance definitions to remain undocumented.
Promise the requested feature immediately to preserve the relationship.
Gather targeted feedback to identify the outcome gap and agree on corrective priorities with customer representatives.
questions.rationale: Scope completion does not guarantee customer value; the project manager should respond to evidence about the customer experience. The best response is to gather targeted feedback to identify the outcome gap and agree on corrective priorities with customer representatives.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: The government tax-filing portal must meet the statutory filing season while protecting security, accessibility, and high-volume demand. Operations accepts the new system technically but has not agreed on ownership, staffing, support levels, or performance measures. The sponsor has asked the team to protect the committed date. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Ignore incentives that reward the old behavior.
Measure adoption only by whether the system was installed.
Treat resistance as a communication failure without investigating causes.
Facilitate operational transition planning and obtain agreement on the future operating model and readiness criteria.
questions.rationale: Organizational change requires a workable operating model, not only technical handoff. The best response is to facilitate operational transition planning and obtain agreement on the future operating model and readiness criteria.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: A project manager is leading the electronic medical records migration. Market research shows that customer demand has shifted toward a different outcome than the current backlog emphasizes. A recent stakeholder survey shows declining confidence. What should the project manager do first?
options: Protect the original backlog even when market evidence changes expected value.
Review the external environment only at project kickoff.
Copy a competitor feature without assessing strategy, value, or risk.
Reassess the business value and reprioritize scope or backlog with stakeholders using current evidence.
questions.rationale: Market change can invalidate earlier value assumptions even when delivery remains on plan. The best response is to reassess the business value and reprioritize scope or backlog with stakeholders using current evidence.
questions.source_note: Original practice item independently authored for this simulation pack.

questions.stem: During the mine rehabilitation initiative, what is the most appropriate management response to the benefits exhibit?
options: Declare success because feature completion is high.
Wait until project closure before reviewing benefits.
Reassess the value assumptions and usage drivers, assign a benefits owner, and adjust priorities using outcome evidence.
Increase scope so the team reaches 100 percent feature completion.
questions.rationale: The outcome is below its target trajectory and has no accountable owner. Value management should investigate causes, clarify ownership, and adapt priorities rather than equating feature completion with benefits.

Point 5 signals a potential special cause that should be investigated.

questions.stem: The telecom network expansion must meet a spectrum-license milestone while protecting permits, equipment supply, and field safety. The team has enough people but lacks the security expertise required for an upcoming compliance milestone. What should the project manager do next to address the situation?
options: Update the resource plan and verify that the selected option meets quality and timing requirements.
Identify the skill gap and decide whether to train, acquire, or borrow the capability in time for the need.
Remove quality or compliance work to fit the available resources.
Keep an infeasible schedule and rely on overtime during execution.
Add headcount without checking whether the required skill is present.
questions.rationale: Resource planning concerns capability as well as headcount. The strongest pair is to identify the skill gap and decide whether to train, acquire, or borrow the capability in time for the need. and then update the resource plan and verify that the selected option meets quality and timing requirements.

questions.stem: A project manager is leading the digital onboarding service for a retail bank. An audit is approaching, but evidence is scattered across personal files and several controls have no documented owner. The sponsor has asked the team to protect the committed date. Which action should the project manager take before proceeding?
options: Create a controlled compliance evidence plan and repository with ownership, traceability, review, and retention rules.
Delegate compliance entirely to legal or audit teams and remove it from project planning.
Keep personal data indefinitely because storage is inexpensive.
Treat AI bias, data lineage, and human oversight as optional technical preferences.
questions.rationale: Compliance must be demonstrable through reliable evidence, not assumed from informal activity. The best response is to create a controlled compliance evidence plan and repository with ownership, traceability, review, and retention rules.

questions.stem: On the customer-support AI assistant, the team is using a predictive life cycle with approved baselines and formal change control. options: Exclude sustainability information because it is not a traditional scope, cost, or schedule measure.
Let teams continue using the original plan after an approved change.
Identify the critical sustainability information and incorporate it into planning and decision criteria.
Select a delivery approach only because the organization used it on the last project.

questions.stem: A project manager is leading the vaccine cold-chain monitoring system. A large solution is planned for one final release even though several components could provide value independently. The project must preserve mandatory compliance and safety outcomes. What should the project manager do first?
options: Treat mandatory compliance work as having no value because customers did not request it.
Keep the original priority order after credible customer evidence changes.
Assess opportunities to deliver the highest-value components incrementally and learn from real use.
Delay all value until the complete solution is finished even when useful increments are possible.
questions.rationale: Incremental delivery can reduce risk, accelerate value, and improve decisions when components are independently useful. The best response is to assess opportunities to deliver the highest-value components incrementally and learn from real use.

questions.stem: During the omnichannel retail launch, which is being delivered through iterative delivery within integrated stage-gate and governance controls, a supplier is missing milestones and quality targets defined in the contract. What should the project manager do first?
options: Review objective performance against the agreement and initiate the documented corrective and escalation process.
Begin supplier work before data, compliance, acceptance, and authority terms are clear.
Use a fixed-price contract when the scope cannot be defined and expect the supplier to absorb all uncertainty.
Select a contract type only because it was used on the previous project.
questions.rationale: Supplier performance should be managed against agreed measures and remedies, not informal impressions. The best response is to review objective performance against the agreement and initiate the documented corrective and escalation process.
